decisions.reason: Confirmed nonfatal normalization inconsistency: for u(x)=x_1 x_2 on a positive-volume subset of R^d, the ordered Hessian sum contributes 2|U| whereas the ordinary W^{2,2} multi-index second-order sum contributes |U|. Retained the explicitly defined Hessian seminorm and full-norm rule and replaced the false identification with the ordinary norm by exact equivalence bounds 1 and sqrt(2); weak mixed derivatives commute distributionally. Membership, real scalars, and every quantitative estimate are preserved.

False positive: the declared affine-simplex/shape-regularity supplier def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes begins “Fix an integer d>=2”; its reference simplex and affine images therefore exclude d=1. F2 invokes reference-simplex smooth density only in this inherited dimension range, matching lem-smooth-density-on-reference-simplex exactly. No unsupported one-dimensional extension is asserted. Checked the variance/Poincare estimate, finite affine orthant extensions, the dyadic trace series with exponent r-1/2>0, homothety and mollification convergence also in the divergence graph norm, Green boundary pairings, and compact-subfacet trace compatibility. The endpoint norm clarification leaves every local seminorm used here unchanged.

False positive: def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes, a direct dependency of this lemma, fixes d>=2 before defining its matching mesh. The global CR space also uses real P1 elements defined only for d>=2. Thus every facet has positive diameter, and h_F^{-1} is defined. In the actual dimension range, affine singular-value bounds give h_F comparable to each incident h_K. An affine zero-mean jump vanishes at the face barycenter; its tangential variation is at most h_F times the adjacent gradients. Squaring, integrating and multiplying by h_F^{-1} gives a cell-volume factor, and each cell is counted at most d+1 times. Boundary facets use just one cell. No item change is warranted.

False positive: d=1 is excluded by the directly imported def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes, whose first defining clause fixes d>=2, and by the real CR local element. For d>=2 the interior link S^{d-1} is connected. Boundary links come from the path-connected local Lipschitz polyhedral epigraph. Avoiding codimension-two faces gives facet chains (for d=2 the circle/arc link has no codimension-two skeleton to avoid). Shape-regular affine maps make the positive-dimensional shared facet diameter comparable to both adjacent cell diameters. The cone-volume argument bounds star cardinality, so bounded chains also bound all size ratios used in Step 3.1. Nodal averaging, finite overlap and zero-extension/cutoff approximation then give both estimates and H^1_0 membership. No one-dimensional interval comparison is used.

Confirmed nonfatal scalar-convention omission: the construction and approved contract use real CR polynomials and real Lax-Milgram, but the theorem never explicitly selected the real branch of its real-or-complex Hilbert/Sobolev suppliers for the continuous problem and datum. If complex values were admitted, a(iw,iw)=-||grad w||^2 and a real CR space could not solve a general imaginary load, so that reading is invalid. Added the intended real-valued datum/Sobolev/L2 convention to Given. This selects the existing real CR formulation rather than replacing its bilinear form. Over R the displayed coercivity constant 1/(1+C_P^2), bounded linear load, real Lax-Milgram, and positive-definite real face-basis matrix are all valid; the zero-dimensional discrete space is explicitly covered.

Confirmed nonfatal omitted boundary branch: on a one-simplex mesh the explicit face-basis supplier gives V_h={0}; the second-Strang Statement defines delta_h^{nc}=0 there, whereas local Step 1.4 displayed its supremum formula without its nonzero-space condition. Added the supplier’s zero-space branch before the quotient, so no empty supremum is asserted. All Strang hypotheses were checked: real Hilbert exact space in the gradient norm, finite Hilbert test space in the comparison norm, bounded loads, extension bound M_h=1 and coercivity alpha_h=(1+C_J)^{-1}. The interpolation and residual estimates still yield the complete comparison-norm rate, also when I_hu=u_h=0. The proof’s final paragraph already establishes an error constant depending only on d, shape regularity and r; Poincare constants establish hypotheses but are absent from the Strang bound.

False positive: F5 expressly cites the energy estimate’s proof, not merely its weaker Statement. That proof’s Step 3.1 already states and establishes dependence only on d, shape regularity and r: the Strang coefficient uses M_h=1 and alpha_h=(1+C_J)^{-1}, while the approximation/residual constants are local; domain-dependent Poincare constants are used only to verify bounded loads and completeness. The zero-space repair preserves this stronger argument. In the L2 proof the cell Green identity has the correct sign; error jumps have zero face means; normal-trace mean subtraction gives h^s times the h^r error-jump bound; the volume split gives the actual discrete consistency residual, not an unjustified orthogonality claim. The smoothing bound then supplies exactly C_reg, and division occurs only after e!=0 is separated. Thus the stated C dependencies and rate h^{r+s} are proved without altering the claim.
